chapter: Kid Thomas band and dance work
title: Kid Thomas never drank; Twat's drinks docked from his pay
summary: Thomas never drank on the bandstand; one rainy night in the Morel room he docked Twat's pay for drinks; Bocage played for the pleasure.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Thomas told me the last time I was talking with him, he told me they was in uh... Twat got drunk in Minnesota, I think it was, and... Said they had to rush him to the doctor. Say, got a fool with that wine out there in Minnesota there and said, Twat fell out on the bass there. Mm. Said they had to take him to the doctor. Well, does he drink any more? I don't know, I never asked Thomas do he still drink, but see Thomas was a boy, he... Thomas never drank it. Mm-hmm. I never seen Thomas took a drink for the whole time I played with him. Cause uh... He used to play them dancers like that, they'd always set a quart of whiskey or so up on the bandstand. But Thomas would bring him a little bottle on it. Go hissing him a little bottle and can't hum. But he'd never drink. He'd never drink on the bandstand. But wash, wash you drink, wash you drink and beg everybody come along for a cigarette. Thomas used to fuss with him all night about that.
Why did he do that? He didn't have any money?

Oh, I don't know, wash was something. One night we was playing, we went to play a dance up in the Morel Room. Me and Thomas and them and rain started pouring down that night. So, wash he told me, he said, come on let's go back there and get something to drink, you know. Get something to eat. I said, no man, I ain't going back there and get nothing to drink. Well, every time wash met back there and got something to drink, the woman marked it down. So, finally the rain stopped and we start the playing. And the hall got crowded. So, when they got ready to pay off, the woman told him, say, well, Thomas, say wash your four dollars. Say, for drinks you need, Thomas. Say, yeah, all right. Say, just give me the money. So, when we got on the bandstand and Thomas start paying off, he told wash, now you don't get a nickel. He said, you don't get nothing. Because he said, you didn't let that drink of yours. And wash went to cry. I'm going to get home. Thomas said, I learned you a lesson by going up there getting drinks without anybody telling you about it. So, well, we all chipped in and give him something to go home with. But wash that didn't drink there's enough. Yeah. Well, at that time, he didn't, like I said, he didn't make no money. You mean, we went out there more so for the pleasure of it. Me, I was there. I didn't care. If I made five or six dollars that night playing, I was satisfied. I didn't care. Just so long I was out there playing.
